# pipeflow

{pipeflow} is a lightweight framework for building interactive data
analysis pipelines in R. You add R functions one by one as steps, tell
{pipeflow} which steps they take their inputs from, and it keeps the
pipeline consistent as you insert, replace or remove steps.

![cartoon](reference/figures/cartoon.png)

### Why pipeflow?

- concise API: steps are plain R functions
- all parameters in one place
- checked as you build
- reruns only what changed
- fast: data.table and C++ DAG under the hood
- feature rich: views, split/map/reduce, nested pipelines

### Installation

``` r

# Install release version from CRAN
install.packages("pipeflow")

# Install development version from GitHub
devtools::install_github("rpahl/pipeflow")
```

### Cheat sheet

[![pipeflow cheat sheet, page
1](reference/figures/cheatsheet-1.png)![pipeflow cheat sheet, page
2](reference/figures/cheatsheet-2.png)](https://github.com/rpahl/pipeflow/blob/main/cheatsheet/pipeflow-cheatsheet.pdf)

### Usage

``` r

library(pipeflow)

p <- pip_new("demo") |>
    pip_add("numbers", \(n = 5) seq_len(n)) |>
    pip_add("squared", \(x = ~numbers) x^2) |>
    pip_add("total", \(x = ~squared) sum(x))

p
# <pipeflow> demo (3 steps)
# -------------------------
#       step params depends state
# 1: numbers      n           new
# 2: squared      x numbers   new
# 3:   total      x squared   new
# -------------------------
# <ready> last run: never

pip_run(p)
# info [2026-10-25 16:44:38.543 UTC]: Starting run of pipeflow 'demo'
# info [2026-10-25 16:44:38.543 UTC]: Step 1/3 numbers
# info [2026-10-25 16:44:38.549 UTC]: Step 2/3 squared
# info [2026-10-25 16:44:38.553 UTC]: Step 3/3 total
# info [2026-10-25 16:44:38.554 UTC]: Finished in 0.012 s (3 done, 0 skipped, 0 failed)

pip_collect(p)
# $numbers
# [1] 1 2 3 4 5
# 
# $squared
# [1]  1  4  9 16 25
# 
# $total
# [1] 55
```

# Package index

## Getting started

Create a pipeline, add steps, and collect results.

- [`pipeflow`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/pipeflow-package.md)
  [`pipeflow-package`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/pipeflow-package.md)
  : pipeflow: Fast Interactive Data Analysis Pipelines
- [`pip_new()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/pip_new.md)
  : Create a pipeline
- [`pip_add()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/pip_add.md)
  : Add a step
- [`pip_collect()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/pip_collect.md)
  : Collect step outputs

## Modify steps

Replace, rename, remove, reset, or re-configure steps.

- [`pip_replace()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/pip_replace.md)
  : Replace a step
- [`pip_rename()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/pip_rename.md)
  : Rename a step
- [`pip_remove()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/pip_remove.md)
  : Remove a step
- [`pip_reset()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/pip_reset.md)
  : Reset a pipeline to its initial state
- [`pip_get_params()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/pip_set_params.md)
  [`pip_set_params()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/pip_set_params.md)
  : Get or set unbound parameters

## Pipeline composition

Combine or clone pipelines, or turn a pipeline into a function.

- [`rbind(`*`<pipeflow>`*`)`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/rbind.pipeflow.md)
  : Bind pipelines
- [`pip_clone()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/pip_clone.md)
  : Clone a pipeline
- [`as.function(`*`<pipeflow>`*`)`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/as.function.pipeflow.md)
  : Turn a pipeline into a function
- [`pip_inner()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/pip_inner.md)
  : Inner pipelines of a pipeline function step

## Running pipelines

Execute pipeline steps or views.

- [`pip_run()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/pip_run.md)
  : Run a pipeline
- [`pip_run_state()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/pip_run_state.md)
  : Get the run state of a pipeline
- [`pip_param_value()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/pip_param_value.md)
  [`` `pip_param_value<-`() ``](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/pip_param_value.md)
  : Annotated parameter values
- [`pip_output_value()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/pip_output_value.md)
  : Annotated step outputs
- [`pipeflow_lgr()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/pipeflow_lgr.md)
  : Default logger of pipeflow

## Locking and tagging

Lock steps against changes or tag them for filtering.

- [`pip_lock()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/pip_lock.md)
  [`pip_unlock()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/pip_lock.md)
  : Lock or unlock steps
- [`pip_tag()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/pip_tag.md)
  [`pip_untag()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/pip_tag.md)
  : Add or remove tags

## Inspection and views

Inspect the pipeline structure, access the step table, and create
filtered views.

- [`pip_view()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/pip_view.md)
  : Create a pipeline view
- [`pip_data()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/pip_data.md)
  : Access the underlying step table
- [`pip_graph()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/pip_graph.md)
  : Build pipeline graph data

## Extract and replace operators

Subset, read from and write to a pipeline using base R operators.

- [`` `[`( ``*`<pipeflow>`*`)`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/Extract.pipeflow.md)
  [`` `[[`( ``*`<pipeflow>`*`)`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/Extract.pipeflow.md)
  [`` `[[<-`( ``*`<pipeflow>`*`)`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/Extract.pipeflow.md)
  [`` `[<-`( ``*`<pipeflow>`*`)`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/Extract.pipeflow.md)
  [`` `$`( ``*`<pipeflow>`*`)`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/Extract.pipeflow.md)
  [`` `$<-`( ``*`<pipeflow>`*`)`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/Extract.pipeflow.md)
  : Extract or replace parts of a pipeline

## S3 methods

Generic methods for pipeflow objects.

- [`length(`*`<pipeflow>`*`)`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/dim.pipeflow.md)
  [`dim(`*`<pipeflow>`*`)`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/dim.pipeflow.md)
  : Dimensions of a pipeflow pipeline or view
- [`str(`*`<pipeflow>`*`)`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/print.md)
  [`print(`*`<pipeflow>`*`)`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/print.md)
  : Print pipeflow objects

# Articles

### All vignettes

- [Get started with
  pipeflow](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/articles/v01-get-started.md):

  Start here if this is your first time using pipeflow.

- [Modify existing
  pipelines](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/articles/v02-modify-pipeline.md):

  How to insert, replace, and remove steps in a pipeline.

- [Combine
  pipelines](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/articles/v03a-combine-pipelines.md):

  How to combine different pipelines to a single pipeline.

- [Pipeline
  views](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/articles/v03b-pipeline-views.md):

  How to filter pipelines with
  [`pip_view()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/reference/pip_view.md)
  and the `[` operator, compose views, and run only a subset of steps.

- [Collect and group
  output](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/articles/v04-collect-output.md):

  How to collect and group pipeline output.

- [Split, map, and
  reduce](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/articles/v05a-split-map-reduce.md):

  Shows how to split data, apply the pipeline to each subset, and then
  reduce the results back into a combined output.

- [Nested
  pipelines](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/articles/v05b-nested-pipeline.md):

  Shows how to run a pipeline as a step of another pipeline with
  as.function(), so that changing its parameters re-executes the outer
  step and only the inner steps that are affected.

- [Handling
  failures](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/articles/v05c-error-handling.md):

  Shows what happens when a step fails, how to keep a pipeline running
  with on_error = “continue”, how to react to failed inputs with ~try()
  references, and how to recover once the cause is fixed.

- [Annotated parameter
  values](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/articles/v05d-param-value.md):

  Shows how to store annotated values (e.g. values with units or labels)
  as step parameters and how to unwrap them right before a step function
  is called, using the pip_param_value() generic.

- [Annotated step
  outputs](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/articles/v05e-output-value.md):

  Shows how to annotate the output of a step when the step returns, for
  example to stamp a result with the step it came from and the time it
  was computed, using the pip_output_value() generic.

- [Self-modifying
  pipelines](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/articles/v06-self-modify-pipeline.md):

  Shows how you can setup pipelines to modify themselves at runtime,
  which, for example, allows for changing pipeline parameters based on
  intermediate results or even dynamically modify the pipeline’s own
  structure during a pipeline run.

- [Comparison and
  benchmarks](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/articles/v07-vs-targets.md):

  Comparing general properties and performance of {pipeflow} vs
  {targets} in a scoped latency comparison.

- [Emulating targets
  features](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/dev/articles/v07b-emulate-targets.md):

  Recipes that emulate features of {targets} with existing {pipeflow}
  functions and a few lines of R code, and where the emulation stops.
